title: Structured-output constraint & schema sanity test suite
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We currently lack a comprehensive, CI-gated test suite that validates structured-output behavior across streaming, function/tool calling, and compatibility adapter layers. This causes intermittent production regressions when models or runtime optimizations change (quantization, kernel swaps, batching).

Goal: Build a reusable test harness and canonical fixture set that verifies: (1) JSON mode enforcement and constrained-decoding accuracy, (2) schema adherence for both final and incremental (streamed) outputs, and (3) compatibility layer behavior for older SDK/client configurations. The suite must run deterministically in CI and produce clear failure signals tied to PRs and rollout dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test harness that runs under CI and exits non-zero on regressions
Coverage across 3 model families (bert-style seq2seq, decoder-only open model v1/v2, and a quantized 8-bit variant)
Tests validate both immediate (single response) and streamed partial-chunk outputs against schemas
Constrained-decoding tests include token-level rejection cases, fallback behavior, and malformed-output detection
Compatibility adapters tested: old-sdk (pre-structured-output), jsonmode-legacy, and streaming-with-legacy-hooks
Clear error codes and console alert links for any failing regression (must include PR link and failing fixture ID)
Automated flakiness detector that re-runs failed cases up to 3x and annotates flaky vs deterministic failures
implementation_notes: Create fixtures as small JSON files under tests/structured_fixtures with: schema, prompt template, expected canonical output, and tolerated deviations
Harness will call Redwood SDK with toggles: json_mode=true/false, constrained_decoding_profile=(strict,balanced,permissive), streaming=true/false, tool_calling_sim=true/false
For streaming validation, reconstruct incremental JSON by appending partial chunks and validate intermediate parseability + final schema compliance
Implement a lightweight 'adapter simulator' that emulates older clients that send legacy 'function_call' and receive non-structured text; ensure runtime fallback is correct
Use deterministic seeds for sampling/temperature and pin tokenizers and max_length in CI runs to avoid nondeterminism
Instrument tests to capture KV cache hits/misses and batching statistics for each run to help triage performance-induced regressions
Expose an opt-in nightly sweep that runs a broader fuzzing corpus to catch edgecases not in CI unit suite
test_plan: Phase 1: Define 24 canonical fixtures covering: valid/invalid JSON, nested objects, arrays, enums, optional fields, and streaming-chunk boundaries
Phase 2: Build harness that can run each fixture against a matrix of: {streaming on/off} x {json_mode strict/balanced} x {tool_calling simulated/none} x {compat_adapter on/off}
Phase 3: Integrate harness into PR CI with an eventual merge gating policy for core-api changes
Phase 4: Create dashboard tiles showing pass/fail by fixture, recent regressions, and top failing PRs
Phase 5: Run compatibility suite against Dedicated and Private deployment images to ensure no environment-specific regressions
Phase 6: Post-merge monitoring: when a test fails in canary, open a rollback-blocking incident with pre-filled triage checklist
